full_judgment:
5. The respondent No.2 entered appearance and filed affidavit-in-opposition denying the material allegation of the writ petitions contending, inter alia, that after receiving the application praying for tax holiday, the National Board of Revenue went for inspection of the factory and found that the petitioner company installed 45 units of used and old machineries along with 94 new machineries and did not produce the material documents during inspection of the same before the Deputy Commissioner of Taxes, Companies Circle- 3, Taxes Zone-1, Dhaka. It is further contended that the petitioner's declaration in respect of the Letter of Credit opened in September, 1999 is not correct because the petitioner opened Letter of Credit on 31-5-99 and 17-8-99 and the declaration as to installation of machineries in January, 2000 and commercial production stated from 1st of April, 2000 are also not correct, because the petitioner commenced its commercial production through old and new machineries at least 3/4 months earlier than the disclosed date of commencement of commercial production and hence the National Board of Revenue was legally justified to reject the prayer for tax exemption under section 46A of the IT Ordinance, 1984. It is further contended by the respondent that the petitioner's company neither submitted application praying for tax holiday in the prescribed form furnishing all the necessary information and documents in this regard for installation of the factory nor disclosed the actual date of commencement of commercial production. The petitioner failed to submit application before the NBR within 180 days as stipulated time limit for praying for tax holiday. Since the .petitioners submitted application after the expiry of 180 days, the NBR was legally justified to reject the prayer of tax holiday. The respondent further contended that the petitioner did not fulfil the condition of section 46(2)(d) and the application for tax holiday was barred by limitation. The National Board of Revenue rejected the application praying for tax holiday after examining the documents produced before it and never took any decision before issuing impugned letter dated 21-12-2000 by which the NBR refused to grant tax holiday for non fulfillment of the terms and conditions as laid down in the concerned provision of law. It is further contended that after receiving the review application by the respondent No.1 it was referred to the 3-member review committee on 11-1-2001. Thereafter, on the application of the petitioner company the NBR arranged hearing for the petitioner before the 3- member review committee on 5-2-2001 which maintained the earlier orders of rejection and accordingly, informed the decision to the petitioner by letter dated 4-4-2001. Thus, on compliance of different provisions of the Ordinance and on perusal, and consideration of all the papers and documents produced before the NBR the rejection order was rightly passed, since the petitioner failed to comply with the terms and conditions of section 46A(2)(d) and 46A(2)(f) of the Ordinance. 

 6. During the hearing of the Rule the respondent No.2 filed a supplementary affidavit and contended that the Deputy Commissioner of Taxes, Circle-3, Zone-1, Dhaka conducted the inspection of the concerned factories for the purpose of exemption and submitted his enquiry report on 19-10-2000 wherein in item No.9 it was stated that out of 139 machineries 45 machineries in total are too old and he also stated that the petitioner company failed to produce the letter of credit, bill of entry, invoice and list of the machineries. The DCT in his report further stated at paragraph Nos. 10(a) and 10(b) that the petitioner company started commercial production with the help of old machineries much earlier in 1999 but in the tax holiday application the petitioner company declared that the company started its commercial production on 1-4-2000 i.e. after about one and half years from the actual date of its commencement of commercial production. This is also reflected from the consumption of electricity bill noted in the order-sheet of the NBR. Upon perusing the electricity bill of September, 1999 to July 2001 the said Deputy Commissioner of Taxes opined that the chronological billing amount proves that the petitioner company started its commercial production with the help of the old machineries more than 6 months ago and hence the petitioner's prayer for tax exemption is barred by limitation. The said DCT also observed that huge number of old machineries are being used in the petitioners' factories. The petitioner company neither submitted all import documents in support of machineries installed in the factories nor disclosed the actual date of commercial production and hence it is observed that the petitioner company did not fulfil the terms and conditions of section 46(2)(d) and (f) of the Ordinance. It is stated in the supplementary affidavit-in-opposition that though the Second Secretary in his note No.11 dated 17-12-2000 and in note No.17 dated 19-12-2000 gave opinion to allow exemption in favour of the petitioner but their opinions were not accepted by the higher authority of the NBR and thus, the same were rejected by letter dated 21-12-2000. Relying on these statements the respondent prays for discharging the Rule since the petitioner did not comply with the terms and conditions of section 46A of the Ordinance for tax holiday.
